(Colorado Springs, Colorado) | college = * [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] (2020–2023) * [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] (2023–2025) | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] ([[2023–24 Mountain West Conference men's basketball season|2024]]) }} '''Dominique Akai "Nique" Clifford''' (born February 9, 2002) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]] of the [[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC) as well as the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Clifford grew up in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] and attended [[The Vanguard School (Colorado)|The Vanguard School]].{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/vanguard-schools-nique-clifford-grew-into-role-as-colorados-star-basketball-prospect-paul-klee/article_aaff7fde-3652-11ea-80b6-07f953740f36.html|title=Vanguard School's Nique Clifford grew into role as Colorado's star basketball prospect|first=Paul|last=Klee|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=January 13, 2020|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He was named the Colorado Gatorade Player of the Year as a senior after averaging 26.3 points, 13.7 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 3.5 steals, and 2.8 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/03/26/dominique-clifford-gatorade-colorado-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/|title=Vanguard’s Dominique Clifford named Gatorade Colorado boys basketball player of the year|first=Joe|last=Nguyen|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=March 26, 2020|access-date=October 29, 2024}} Clifford committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Denver Pioneers men's basketball|Denver]], [[Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball|Northern Colorado]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], and [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]].{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/vanguards-nique-clifford-commits-to-university-of-colorado-basketball/article_f6e5baf8-dbe9-11e9-97f4-5f8cf0eda8e0.html|title=Vanguard's Nique Clifford commits to University of Colorado basketball|first=Lindsey|last=Smith|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=September 20, 2019|access-date=October 29, 2024}} ==College career== Clifford began his college career playing for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]].{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2021/06/11/adjusting-to-bench-life-a-season-long-learning-experience-for-cu-buffs-nique-clifford/|title=Adjusting to bench life a season-long learning experience for CU Buffs' Nique Clifford|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=June 11, 2021|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He averaged 6.7 points and 4.6 rebounds during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.timescall.com/2023/11/29/game-day-notes-nique-clifford-awaits-old-teammates-in-huge-cu-csu-showdown/|title=Game day notes: Nique Clifford awaits old teammates in huge CU-CSU showdown|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[Longmont Daily Times-Call]]|date=November 29, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} As a junior, Clifford played in 35 games with 33 starts and averaged 5.9 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.timescall.com/2024/03/20/former-cu-buff-nique-clifford-continues-bounce-back-season-for-csu-rams/|title=Former CU Buff Nique Clifford continues bounce-back season for CSU Rams|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[Longmont Daily Times-Call]]|date=March 20, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} After the season, Clifford entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/cu-buffs-nique-clifford-says-chase-for-nba-dream-played-large-role-in-transfer-portal/article_bde5bc7a-ca7f-11ed-a334-738d8c3bb731.html|title=CU Buffs' Nique Clifford says chase for NBA dream played large role in transfer portal decision|first=Luke|last=Zahlmann|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} Clifford transferred to [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2023/04/23/nique-clifford-transfer-colorado-state-basketball-from-cu/70136682007/|title=Colorado basketball transfer Nique Clifford to transfer to Colorado State|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=April 23, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He averaged 12.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, and three assists and was named third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] in his first season with the Rams.{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2024/05/30/nique-clifford-withdraws-from-nba-draft-returns-to-colorado-state-basketball-team/73887837007/|title=Nique Clifford withdraws from NBA draft, returns to Colorado State men's basketball team|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=May 30, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} In his final year of eligibility, Clifford was named first-team and defensive team All-Mountain West. {{cite web|url=https://themw.com/news/2025/03/11/mountain-west-announces-2024-25-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams/|title=Mountain West Announces 2024-25 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|website=[[Mountain West Conference]]|date=March 11, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} On March 7, 2025, Clifford scored a career-high 36 points in a 83-73 victory against the [[Boise State Broncos]] in his final regular season game. {{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2025/03/07/nique-clifford-leads-colorado-state-basketball-to-win-at-boise-state/81932117007/|title=Epic Nique Clifford performance leads Colorado State basketball to huge win at Boise State|website=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=March 8, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} On March 15, 2025, Clifford was named the [[2025 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament]] MVP after he led the Rams with 24 points against Boise State Broncos in the championship game. {{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/mountain-west-championship-score-39c80d39e2d2ec8e3bc85562744b9c2a#:~:text=LAS%20VEGAS%20(AP)%20%E2%80%94%20Nique,its%20first%20title%20since%202003.|title=Clifford scores 24, Colorado State hits record 12 3s to beat Boise State 69-56 in MWC Championship|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 15, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} ==References== {{Reflist}}
